name: Single Permit (Employed Work)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a confirmed job offer from a Greek employer, who must initiate the invitation/hiring procedure with the competent authority.

The position and specialty must fall within the maximum-numbers Joint Ministerial Decision issued every two years under Article 11 of Law 4251/2014, setting quotas for third-country workers by region and specialty.

evidence_required.document: Work visa from Greek consular authority (for those applying from abroad)

outcome.duration_length: not specified in sources reviewed for the general single permit (seasonal work capped at up to 9 months per 12-month period, extendable to 5 years total, is a distinct sub-category)

sources.title: Greek Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs -- Work for third-country nationals in Greece (biennial quota system, employer-initiated procedure, single permit)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Greece's initial build. Confirmed directly at tier-1 (Ministry of Labour): a mandatory biennial quota system under Article 11 of Law 4251/2014 gates most employer-sponsored work, alongside the employer-initiated invitation procedure. Also note Law 5275/2026 (published 6 February 2026, per EY Greece, tier-3) introduced several new specialised short-term work/visa categories (EU Blue Card validity extended to 3 years; a 12-month Tech Visa for Elevate-Greece-registered startup employees; a post-study 1-year job-search permit for graduates/researchers; visiting-professor and graduate-jobs visas) -- these are recent enough that this pass did not independently verify each at tier-1 beyond the EY summary, and are not modelled as separate route files here to avoid fragmenting the dataset on unconfirmed specifics; flagged for a future revisit once the underlying gazette text is checked. EU Blue Card itself also not modelled as its own separate route in this pass -- it is a distinct legal category from the general single permit and should be added once specifically researched.
